contradictions.what: Rep says 'nothing bombed, good cycle, lost on price', but admits no customer-specific value figure and nothing from us for Martin on cost of failed orders.
Rep says the rate killed it and more rate room wins, but also concedes Martin would still see 'same rate, so why move' and the IT lead was hesitant.
Rep says Lucy was sold and loved the pitch, yet she asked for a one-page business case for Martin and received only generic deck and pricing.
Lucy said approval was a formality and IT was fine, but the CFO refused; the rep never met the decider and relies on Lucy.
Rep says 'same thing' is not true, but our materials never put the differences (gateway fee, chargebacks, declines) in front of Martin.
Rep says IT was fine with it, but later says IT lead was nervous about moving before spring and only conditional on finance approval.

dodges.question: Which part of our pitch got a reaction, and which got silence?
dodges.what: Answered 'Silence, honestly, nothing bombed' and moved to 'we lost on price'; named no silent part.

dodges.question: So what did Martin have in front of him about what one in twelve orders was costing?
dodges.what: Hesitated, said 'Nothing from us', then assumed Lucy told him; contradicts the earlier 'good cycle' framing.

dodges.question: Did we put a figure on the value they'd get?
dodges.what: Answered with the generic uplift slide; admitted no Fernbrook figure only when pressed.

dodges.question: What did they ask for that we couldn't show?
dodges.what: Described the business case request but framed sending deck and pricing as the response.
